info.title: Journal API
info.description:
API for the tasks, notebooks, and notes of a single user.

Every route requires a device token, except login (`POST /devices`). The token comes from logging in with the master password, belongs to one device, and does not expire; it stops working only when the device is revoked with `DELETE /devices/{id}` or `DELETE /devices/current`. Without a token, or with an unknown or revoked one, the response is 401 with the `WWW-Authenticate` header, even on routes that do not exist.

Clients that store the token themselves, such as native apps and terminals, send it in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Browsers log in with `token_delivery: cookie` and the API keeps the token in an `HttpOnly` cookie. When a request has both, the `Authorization` header wins. A request that authenticates with the cookie and uses `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE` must come from the same origin (`Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`), or it gets 403.

Request bodies need `Content-Type: application/json`. In any writable field, `null` is the same as omitting the field. Unknown or read-only fields (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`) are rejected with 400, even with a `null` value.

Errors follow RFC 9457 (`application/problem+json`). A route that does not exist responds 404. An unsupported method on an existing route responds 405 with the `Allow` header.

get.description: Returns every task that is not deleted, ordered by `priority` ascending, then `created_at` descending, then `id` ascending. There are no filters and no pagination.

200.description: List of tasks, empty when there are none.

post.description: Creates a task with a server-generated ID (UUIDv7). Omitted fields get the default values.

put.description:
Upsert with a client-chosen ID.

If the ID does not exist, creates the task (201). If it exists, replaces the whole task (200): omitted or `null` fields go back to the default, and `created_at` is kept. If the ID belongs to a deleted task, responds 409.

201.description: Task created with the given ID.

409.description: The ID belongs to a deleted task. Deleted tasks are not restored.

patch.description:
Changes only the fields sent. `null` fields are ignored, and `description: ""` clears the description.

Any field present updates `updated_at`, even when the value does not change. A body without fields (`{}` or only `null`) returns the task unchanged.

delete.description: Soft delete. The task then responds 404 on every endpoint and leaves the list. There is no restore.

get.description: Returns every notebook that is not archived, in creation order (`created_at` ascending, then `id` ascending). There are no filters and no pagination.

200.description: List of notebooks, empty when there are none.

post.description: Creates a notebook with a server-generated ID (UUIDv7).

put.description: Upsert with a client-chosen ID. If the ID does not exist, creates the notebook (201). If it exists, changes the name (200) and keeps `created_at`. If the ID belongs to an archived notebook, responds 409.

201.description: Notebook created with the given ID.

409.description: The ID belongs to an archived notebook, or another active notebook already has the name.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: A notebook named Plants already exists.

patch.description: Changes only the fields sent. A body without fields (`{}` or only `null`) returns the notebook unchanged.

delete.description:
Soft delete, even when the notebook has notes. The notebook then responds 404, leaves the list, and frees its name for another notebook. There is no unarchive.

The notebook's notes do not change: they stay reachable through `/notes/{id}`, but `GET /notes?notebook=` with this notebook responds 404.

get.description:
Returns the notes of a notebook that are not deleted, newest first, 50 per page. The notebook is required: no timeline mixes notebooks.

The order is `date` descending by the start of the period, then the finer precision first, then `created_at` descending, then `id` descending. A coarse-precision note sits at the start of its period: `2026-08-04` → `2026-08` → `2026-05-10T10:30` → `2026-05` → `2026`.

When there are more notes, the `Link` header (RFC 8288) carries the next page with `rel="next"`. The last page has no `Link`. Pagination stays stable even when notes are created or deleted between pages.

post.description: Creates a note with a server-generated ID (UUIDv7).

put.description: Upsert with a client-chosen ID. If the ID does not exist, creates the note (201). If it exists, replaces `notebook_id`, `content`, and `date` (200) and keeps `created_at`; changing `notebook_id` moves the note to another notebook. If the ID belongs to a deleted note, responds 409.

201.description: Note created with the given ID.

409.description: The ID belongs to a deleted note. Deleted notes are not restored.

patch.description:
Changes only the fields sent. `null` fields are ignored. Changing `notebook_id` moves the note to another notebook. Changing `date` may change the precision (e.g. from `2025-07-18T15:35` to `2025-07`).

Any field present updates `updated_at`. A body without fields (`{}` or only `null`) returns the note unchanged.

delete.description: Soft delete. The note then responds 404 on every endpoint and leaves the timeline. There is no restore.

post.description:
Checks the master password and creates a device with a new token. The token appears only in this response; the server keeps only its hash. The request's `User-Agent` is stored on the device.

After 5 wrong passwords in 15 minutes, the client IP gets 429 until the oldest failure leaves the window, even with the right password. The IP is the last entry of `X-Forwarded-For`, which the reverse proxy fills. Successful logins do not count.

201.description: Device authenticated. With `token_delivery: body`, the body carries the token. With `token_delivery: cookie`, the body has no token and `Set-Cookie` carries it.

schema.description: The token cookie: `__Secure-journal_token=<token>; Path=/api; Max-Age=34560000; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict`.

403.description: `token_delivery` is `cookie`, but the request does not come from the same origin (`Sec-Fetch-Site` is not `same-origin`).

example.title: Forbidden
example.detail: Cross-site requests cannot use the token cookie.

get.description: Returns every device with access, in login order. The device that made the request has `current` set to true. Tokens never appear.
Returns the device whose token authenticated the request. A browser can call it at startup to learn whether its cookie is still valid.

delete.description: Revokes the device whose token authenticated the request and expires the token cookie.

Set-Cookie.description: Expires the token cookie (`__Secure-journal_token=; Max-Age=0`) when the revoked device is the calling one.

schema.description: Expires the token cookie (`__Secure-journal_token=; Max-Age=0`) when the revoked device is the calling one.

delete.description: Deletes the device, and its token stops working at once. With the ID of the calling device, it works as a logout, like `DELETE /devices/current`.

PartialDate.description:
An approximate moment in local time, without time zone, in reduced-precision ISO 8601. The format gives the precision: `YYYY` (year), `YYYY-MM` (month), `YYYY-MM-DD` (day), `YYYY-MM-DDTHH` (approximate hour), or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` (exact minute).

Only the canonical format is accepted: leading zeros, `T` as the separator, no seconds, and no time zone. The date must exist in the calendar and start no later than now, in the server's time zone; so the current year is valid. The year goes from `0001` to `9999`.
